questions.question_text: How many total hours of pre-license education must a Rhode Island salesperson candidate complete?
questions.explanation: Salesperson candidates must complete 45 classroom hours (230-RICR-30-20-2.7(A)) plus a separate 3-hour Lead Paint and Lead Hazard Mitigation course, for 48 hours total. Three of the 45 hours must cover the state agency law.

questions.question_text: A salesperson candidate wants to complete the 45-hour pre-license course through a self-paced online program she can watch whenever she likes. Is this permitted in Rhode Island?
questions.correct_answer: No, pre-license courses cannot be pre-recorded
distractors: Yes, any DBR-approved provider may offer it
No, all pre-license courses must be in person
Yes, if she passes a proctored final exam
questions.explanation: On-demand and pre-recorded instruction is prohibited for pre-licensing courses (230-RICR-30-20-2.7(D)(2)). A live-virtual classroom is allowed — students must be on video and able to interact with the instructor in real time — so remote study itself is not the problem.

questions.question_text: How many hours of pre-licensing education are required for a Rhode Island broker candidate?
questions.explanation: Broker candidates must complete 90 classroom hours (230-RICR-30-20-2.7(B)). The 45 hours used to qualify as a salesperson cannot be counted toward the 90, and hours older than four years do not count.

questions.question_text: A candidate completed the 45-hour salesperson course but skipped the Lead Paint module. What additional course must she complete before sitting for the exam?
questions.explanation: Rhode Island requires a separate 3-hour Lead Paint and Lead Hazard Mitigation course on top of the 45-hour pre-license course. Both must be finished before the candidate is eligible to sit for the exam.

questions.question_text: A candidate finished her 45-hour pre-license course three years ago and is only now applying for a salesperson license. What is the effect?
questions.correct_answer: The hours are too old and must be retaken
distractors: The hours count as long as the school is still approved
She may apply within five years of completing them
She may count half the hours toward the requirement
questions.explanation: Classroom hours completed more than two years before the date of application do not count toward the 45-hour salesperson requirement (230-RICR-30-20-2.7(A)). The broker equivalent runs four years.

questions.question_text: What is the minimum age requirement to obtain a real estate license in Rhode Island?
questions.explanation: Applicants must be at least 18 years of age to obtain a real estate license in Rhode Island. This is consistent with the age requirement in most states.

questions.question_text: A license applicant submits her application with $140. The application is returned as incomplete. What additional fee is required?
questions.explanation: The total application fee is $165 — $140 payable to the General Treasurer plus $25 deposited into the Real Estate Recovery Account before an original license is issued (230-RICR-30-20-2.8(A)). Both must accompany the application.

questions.question_text: A candidate passes the Pearson VUE exam but does not activate her license for 20 months. Is her approved application still valid?
questions.correct_answer: No, exam results expire after one year
distractors: Yes, applications remain valid for 24 months
Only if she pays a late reactivation fee
questions.explanation: Passing results are valid for one year from the passing date, and the application for licensure must be filed within that year. After 20 months her results have expired and she must retake both sections.

questions.question_text: What minimum passing score is required on each section of the Rhode Island real estate licensing exam?
questions.explanation: The passing score on each section is a scaled score of 70. Pearson VUE converts raw scores to a 0-100 scale, so the reported score is neither the number nor the percentage of questions answered correctly.

questions.question_text: An applicant has a prior criminal record. What document must she obtain as part of her Rhode Island license application?
questions.correct_answer: Criminal History Record from the AG Bureau
distractors: Court clearance letter from a local judge
Character reference from a licensed broker
questions.explanation: Rhode Island license applicants must obtain a Criminal History Record from the RI Attorney General's Bureau of Criminal Identification. This is a required part of the application process.

questions.question_text: A salesperson was first licensed in Rhode Island in 2023. When does her license come up for renewal?
questions.correct_answer: Every two years on her license anniversary
distractors: By April 30 of each even-numbered year
On May 1 of each even-numbered year
questions.explanation: Licenses issued after January 1, 2020 renew every two years on the anniversary of the date the license was issued (230-RICR-30-20-2.9(C)). Only licenses issued before that date still renew on May 1 of each even-numbered year.

questions.question_text: How many hours of continuing education must a Rhode Island licensee complete each renewal cycle?
questions.explanation: Licensees must complete 24 clock hours of approved courses every two years (230-RICR-30-20-2.30). At least nine hours must come from the listed core subjects, and at least three of those nine must be fair housing.

questions.question_text: A salesperson leaves Broker A and joins Broker B. What must the salesperson do regarding DBR?
questions.correct_answer: Notify DBR of the broker change
questions.explanation: A licensee must notify DBR in writing of a change in firm affiliation within 10 days (230-RICR-30-20-2.3). The former principal broker reports the disaffiliation and the new principal broker submits a signed transfer-of-license form.

questions.question_text: Effective June 2025, an agent holds both an MLO and RE license. What restriction applies when both roles overlap in a single transaction?
questions.correct_answer: Cannot collect compensation for both roles
distractors: Must disclose but can collect both fees
Must choose which license to surrender
Must have broker approval for dual pay
questions.explanation: A person holding both a mortgage loan originator license and a real estate license cannot be compensated for both roles in the same transaction, effective June 24, 2025. Holding both licenses is still permitted — using both in one deal for pay is not.

questions.question_text: A Rhode Island salesperson let her license expire and did nothing about it for 18 months. What must she do to be licensed again?
questions.correct_answer: Reapply and retake the licensing examination
distractors: Pay a $100 late fee and renew
Complete double the continuing education hours
Wait out a one-year suspension, then renew
questions.explanation: A license that has been expired for more than one year cannot be renewed — the former licensee must file a new application and retake the exam (230-RICR-30-20-2.6(C)). Practicing on an expired license is itself a separate ground for discipline.
